breaking.headline: Stocks rally on Black Friday as AI fears fade
breaking.fact: The S&P 500 climbed about 1.1%, the Nasdaq 1.6% and the Dow roughly 470 points in Friday's shortened Black Friday session, which ends at 1 PM ET, as investors bought back beaten-down AI shares after Wednesday's rout; Nvidia was the odd one out, slipping after a 4.7% premarket pop faded.

breaking.headline: China, Japan and partners hit back at Trump's new tariffs
breaking.fact: China expressed 'firm opposition' to Wednesday's Section 301 tariff proposal and Japan and other partners protested, a day after Washington proposed 20%-40% levies on 14 economies over excess industrial capacity. The U.S. and China also extended their trade truce by two months to Jan. 10, 2027, and the duties would not take effect before February.

breaking.headline: Russia hits two grain ships near Odesa
breaking.fact: Russia attacked two foreign cargo ships carrying more than 100,000 metric tons of grain overnight near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, Prime Minister Sergiy Koretskyi said Thursday. Grain shipments from Odesa have all but stopped since late July as Russia intensified attacks on terminals and vessels, and Moscow ruled out a new Black Sea grain deal at the UN.

breaking.headline: Bush Airport proposes 183-acre cargo expansion
breaking.fact: Houston Airports announced plans to expand George Bush Intercontinental's East Cargo area by 183 acres, from about 100 to 283 acres, to make room for businesses moving goods for the region's energy, aerospace and biotechnology industries. Development proposals are expected in early 2027, with no construction or opening date set.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide traded near €192.06 in Paris on Friday, up about 0.9% from Thursday's €190.32 close, as European shares rallied with Wall Street back from Thanksgiving. At the ECB's Nov 27 reference rate of 1.0957 the quote converts to $210.44, close to the year's high of €194.70. Steady industrial-gas demand and a firm CAC 40 are doing the work, and the Paris close will set the next print.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic jumped 9.1% to $90.34 in Friday's rebound, leading the AI names higher after Wednesday's selloff and back above its $83 IPO price. The math world is still waiting on the Nov 20 Navier-Stokes blow-up claim with NYU's Tristan Buckmaster, whose numerical certificate has yet to be released, so that proof stays unverified. A strong half session could carry the stock into the weekend with momentum.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: The Treasury-bill fund inched up to $91.67 in Friday's session, doing what it is built for while growth stocks whipsaw. Its distribution yield is 4.04%, on a $0.30849-per-share payout made Nov 5. It barely moves day to day, which is the point. With a December hike priced as near-certain and the VIX still above 25, BIL's quiet steadiness stays the point as the tape swings between selloff and rebound.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet was nearly flat at $272.98 in Friday's session, lagging a Nasdaq rally of more than 1.5% after Wednesday's 2.1% drop on hot PCE data and new tariff proposals. There was no Alphabet-specific news behind the drift — the stock is simply not joining the AI rebound the way chips and Anthropic are. The next read comes after the half session, when the tape thins into the weekend.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly eased 0.2% to $1,390.07 on Friday, a quiet session after Wednesday's 1.1% dip gave back part of Tuesday's 3.2% jump. The drugmaker is holding up well through the market's swings, with money still rotating into defensive names when growth wobbles. With the half session thin and the Dow above 50,000, Lilly's next move waits on whether the safety trade holds up.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 1.4% to $306.12 on Friday as energy stayed bid, with Brent near $95.42 and WTI around $84.09 while Gulf shipping attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries keep supply fears high. Tight global gas markets and rising Gulf tensions keep favoring U.S. LNG exporters, and the run looks durable. OPEC+ meets Sunday, with output targets expected to hold into the first quarter.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia slipped 0.8% to $148.10 on Friday, the odd one out in the AI rebound after a 4.7% premarket pop faded at the open. S&P has its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative on governance grounds, and the FT reported Nvidia halted server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations under new U.S. export rules. The stock is still up sharply on the week since Huang's return, but Friday shows the rally is not one-way.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer was essentially flat at $28.46 on Friday, keeping Tuesday's 3.9% gain as investors rotated into defensive dividend payers during the market's wild week. The drugmaker's calm stood out while the Nasdaq plunged intraday Wednesday and then rebounded Friday. With the half session thin, Pfizer's dividend yield keeps it on the safe-haven list heading into the weekend.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 6.1% to $49.88 on Friday, riding the market's risk-on rebound after Wednesday's 2.3% bounce. The space stock is one of the tape's most volatile names, swinging hard with risk appetite as the Nasdaq rallied 1.6%. No company news drove the move — pure sentiment — so the thin half session could bring another sharp swing in either direction before the close.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital gained 1.1% to $9.02 on Friday, extending a strong week as the mortgage REIT's dividend yield pulled in buyers during the market's flight to income. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 4.91% as stocks recover, a friendly backdrop for mortgage REITs. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, the rate path matters most for Rithm's book value and dividend.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: The leveraged S&P 500 fund rose 3.1% to $131.38 on Friday, tracking the market's rally with its usual amplified swing. The S&P climbed about 1.1% in the half session after falling 3.2% intraday Wednesday, so the fund's gain reflects the furious buying rather than a calm day. Leveraged funds cut both ways — a thin session could magnify any late move before the 1 PM ET close.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist added 1.2% to $48.46 on Friday, holding firm as the Dow climbed past 50,600 and banks caught a bid in the holiday rebound. Financials benefited as the 10-year yield held near 4.91% and the market priced a December hike as near-certain. With the session ending at 1 PM ET, the question is whether the Dow can hold above its round-number milestone into the weekend.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony firmed 1.4% to $2.24 on Friday, steadying after a choppy week as small miners caught the risk-on bid. China's export curbs and U.S. critical-mineral policy remain the long-term bull case, but the stock still trades on risk appetite day to day. With futures higher into the half session, the miner could keep steadying if sentiment holds through the early close.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy climbed 4.0% to $5.92 on Friday, leading the watchlist's rebound as risk appetite returned to the tape. Nuclear expansion and U.S. uranium buying remain the structural story, but the stock is tied to sentiment while the Fed's rate path dominates. With oil firm on Gulf tensions and the Nasdaq up 1.6%, the setup favors a steadier session into the early close.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC is estimated at $149.31, up 1.1% on the S&P 500's Friday rally, using the S&P-anchored estimator recalibrated from Dave's account value. The S&P climbed about 1.1% in the shortened session after Wednesday's wild intraday swing, so the estimate reflects the rebound, not the panic low. The next estimate comes after the half session — and a strong close would lift it further into the weekend.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero rose 1.6% to $328.12 on Friday as oil stayed firm, with Brent near $95.42 and WTI around $84.09 after Houthi strikes on Saudi ports and a refinery. Higher crude lifts product prices but squeezes margins, so Valero's direction hinges on how far the supply scare runs. OPEC+ meets Sunday with output targets expected to hold, which should keep the crude backdrop supportive.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV sits at $28.45 as of Nov 25, with the next print coming after Friday's half session. The balanced fund's bond sleeve cushioned Wednesday's intraday plunge, while its equity holdings joined the afternoon rebound and Friday's rally. On a thin, holiday-shortened tape, the fund's next move waits on whether the rebound holds into the early close.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The sweep fund keeps doing its quiet job while the market whipsaws — the VIX is still above 25 after spiking to 28.29 Wednesday. Per the standing plan, balances above $1,000 get swept into CDs, so the position should keep shrinking steadily toward zero.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The Treasury money fund remains the top-yielding cash parking spot on the board, comfortably ahead of Schwab's SWVXX at 3.79% and of most bank savings rates. With a December hike priced as near-certain, money-fund yields should stay firm into the weekend and beyond.

weekInBrief.headline: FCC clears SpaceX's 1-million-satellite orbital data-center plan
weekInBrief.body: The Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday conditionally authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites — the Starmind constellation — to run AI data centers in orbit, the first U.S. authorization of its kind. SpaceX must put its first satellite up by November 2033 and deploy the full constellation by 2040; scientists raised doubts about debris and feasibility, and the FCC has not yet approved debris plans for satellites above 600 km.

weekInBrief.headline: China's CSI 300 jumps 4.2% in its best day since October 2024
weekInBrief.body: China's CSI 300 stock index soared 4.2% Friday, its biggest one-day gain since October 2024, after a rare midday statement by the State Council pledging to boost the role of the stock market. The rally came as Beijing also pushed back on Washington's new tariff proposals, and Chinese shares led a broad Asian rebound while U.S. markets were dark for Thanksgiving.

weekInBrief.headline: ConocoPhillips exits Norway in a $4.4 billion deal with Vår Energi
weekInBrief.body: ConocoPhillips agreed Monday to sell its Norway business and its 40.25% interest in and operatorship of the UK Teesside oil terminal to Vår Energi for $4.425 billion, ending more than half a century on the Norwegian shelf since Phillips discovered Ekofisk in 1969. After adjustments the total consideration is about $3.9 billion, with roughly $2.5 billion in net cash, and the deal is expected to close by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

weekInBrief.headline: Adobe sees $12.9 billion in Black Friday online spending
weekInBrief.body: Adobe Analytics projects U.S. online spending will reach $12.9 billion on Black Friday, up 9.2% from a year ago, with $15.1 billion expected on Cyber Monday. Shoppers have already spent $82.5 billion online since Nov. 1, and retailers say AI-powered shopping tools and cost concerns are steering carts toward necessities as well as gifts.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: On Thursday, a suspected Iranian drone attack on a Kuwaiti military site killed two Italian technicians employed by defense firm Rheinmetall Italia, according to Italy's foreign minister; Iran denied carrying it out. Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery at Ras Tanura on Wednesday, and a Riyadh skyscraper housing the kingdom's sovereign wealth fund was hit for a second time this week, wounding 11 people. The IRGC claimed Friday that a tanker exploded on a mine north of Ghavam Island and a second tanker turned back, but named no vessel and no independent body has confirmed it. CNN's analysis of UKMTO data counts around two dozen attacks on ships in November, nearing October's record 30. Kpler's preliminary data put oil flows through the strait at 55% of pre-war levels over the week to Nov 25, with Iranian loadings still at zero under the blockade — so the oil still moving is non-Iranian Gulf crude under U.S. protection.

space.headline: Dust from the Kuiper belt points to a 'heavy water' reservoir
space.body: Twelve dust grains caught in Earth's upper atmosphere by NASA aircraft and traced to the Kuiper belt carry clay minerals that formed in water loaded with heavy oxygen — about 15.5% more oxygen-18 than Earth's ocean water, NASA and UCLA scientists report in Science Advances. The finding is compelling evidence of a major, chemically distinct reservoir of heavy water beyond the giant planets, apparently kept walled off from the inner solar system, most likely by Saturn and the ice giants.

space.headline: Curiosity finds 'potato chip' crystals on Mars
space.body: NASA's Curiosity rover found bedrock studded with thin, disk-shaped crystal forms — likened to potato chips — while drilling at a site nicknamed Nazca on the slopes of Mount Sharp, and photographed them up close with its MAHLI camera on Nov. 7. The rover fired its ChemCam laser at the crystals and fed drilled samples to its onboard SAM laboratory, but scientists still do not know how the shapes formed or what they are made of.

space.headline: Two AI labs claim the same 47-year-old math proof in one day — neither checked yet
space.body: Anthropic and OpenAI each posted a claimed proof of the same 47-year-old conjecture — VP is not equal to VNP, the algebraic cousin of P vs NP — within hours of each other on Nov. 23, and neither proof has been checked by an outside mathematician. Anthropic's 70-page paper, credited to Claude as sole author, claims a lower bound growing like 2 to the (log n) to the 4/3; OpenAI's first paper claimed a weaker bound, then added nine more manuscripts. Both labs posted Lean formalizations, and the verification queue is now the bottleneck.

space.headline: Drained peatlands account for about 3% of human-caused warming
space.body: Draining the world's peatlands has contributed about 2.7% of present-day human-caused warming, MIT researchers report in Nature, after combining drainage records from 1800 to 2020 with greenhouse-gas models. About 15% of all peatland area — 0.5% of the world's land — has been drained, and the exposed peat keeps releasing carbon dioxide for centuries; even with no further drainage, maintaining today's drained peatlands could nearly double their warming contribution by 2100.

apod.title: Shivelyuch Socked In
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Lauren Dauphin, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey — NASA Earth Observatory Image of the Day, Nov. 27, 2026
apod.explanation: Landsat 9 captured this view of Shivelyuch volcano on Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula on November 8, 2026: clouds ringed the snowy flanks but stayed below the 3,283-meter peak, leaving a clear opening over the 9-kilometer-wide caldera and its dark lava dome. Effusive eruptions and explosive activity at Shivelyuch had been ongoing for months, and on the day of the image a plume of resuspended ash drifted 120 kilometers to the east.
